description: Sync feature flags with their targeting, segments and environments from the LaunchDarkly projects you choose, plus the account's members, teams and audit log.
opening: Sync feature flags, segments and environments from the LaunchDarkly projects you select, plus the account's members, teams and audit log. Each flag, segment, environment, member, team and audit entry is one document. A flag carries its configuration in every environment: on or off, prerequisites, individual targets, rules, the default rollout and its variations.

This is a record of configuration, not live flag evaluation: big-segment membership is not listed, so search cannot tell you every user who gets a variation. Project content follows LaunchDarkly's project view access only when Enforce ACL is on. Members, teams and account-wide audit entries are visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule.

permissions.who_can_read: Access follows the project. Flags, segments, environments and audit entries about one project can be read by the members whose LaunchDarkly role lets them view that project. Reader, Writer, Admin and Owner can view every project. No access views none. A member's own custom role replaces the base role, team roles add to it, and preset role statements, role attributes and permission grants are taken into account. Members, teams and audit entries about the account as a whole are not restricted.
permissions.identity: A member's email address. Members who were invited but have not joined are left out.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot work out who can view a project, or an audit entry touches several projects or all of them, the connector reports a permission warning.
notes: Only project view access counts. Flag-level and environment-level permission statements are not considered.
A project with no viewers, a viewer without an email, or more than 1,000 viewers cannot be captured. Some custom role statements cannot be evaluated either.
For permissions, the token's role must be able to read members, teams and custom roles. The built-in Reader role can.

connect.auth: LaunchDarkly uses an access token. The Reader role is enough.

credentials.name: auth_token
credentials.text: A LaunchDarkly access token, ideally a service token with the Reader role.

permissions.name: Reader
permissions.text: reads projects, environments, flags, segments, members, teams and the audit log. Writer and Admin add only write access, which the connector never uses.

steps.title: Create a service token
steps.text: In LaunchDarkly, open Account settings, Authorization, Access tokens, Create token. Keep the role as Reader. Tick This is a service token, so the token keeps working when the person who made it is deactivated. Copy the token: it is shown once.

steps.title: Select projects
steps.text: HydraDB lists the projects the token can see, by name and key. Select the projects to sync. Members, teams and the audit log are read for the whole account.

connect.account: One connector reads one LaunchDarkly account.

sync.first_sync: Flags, segments and environments of each selected project, and the account's members and teams, are read in full, whatever their age.
sync.changes: Flags, segments, environments, members and teams are read in full on every sync, and ones that did not change are skipped. The audit log is read from the newest entry already synced.
sync.edits: A change to a flag, segment, environment, member or team is picked up on the next sync.
sync.deletes: Items deleted in LaunchDarkly can stay searchable in HydraDB. New links skip items that were deleted.
notes: If LaunchDarkly refuses members, teams or the audit log on the first request, they are skipped. A refusal after some records arrive fails the sync, and so does a rejected token.
If one project is refused, the other projects still sync.
A new LaunchDarkly organization has one empty project and no flags, so a nearly empty first sync is expected.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Feature flags
documents.one_document: One feature flag in one project, with its configuration in every environment.
documents.title: The flag name, else its key.
documents.text: The name and description, then `Kind`, `Project`, `Maintainer` and `Tags` lines, and markers when the flag is temporary or archived. Then one section per environment, in order: on or off, prerequisites, individual user and context targets, rules in order, the default rollout and the off variation. Then each variation's name, value and description. Empty values are left out. A prerequisite's variation can show as a number instead of its name. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: The latest change in any environment, else when the flag was created.
documents.link_back: The flag's targeting page in LaunchDarkly.

attributes.name: flag_key
attributes.text: The flag key. Searchable only when the flag has no name and the key is its title.

attributes.name: maintainer
attributes.text: The maintainer's name, else their email, written as the `Maintainer` line.

attributes.name: maintainer_id
attributes.text: Links the flag to the maintainer's member record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: temporary, archived
attributes.text: Written as markers only when true.

attributes.name: Environment, prerequisite and segment references
attributes.text: Link the flag to each environment it is configured in, each prerequisite flag and each segment its rules match. Not searchable as links.

attributes.name: created_at, last_modified_at
attributes.text: The latest change, else creation, is the result date. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.launchdarkly_flag_key
attributes.text: The flag key. Picks out one flag. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The project key. Limits a query to one project. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The project name. Limits a query to one project by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
attributes.text: Always `project`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Project
attributes.text: The flag's project. Who can view the project decides who can read the flag. Not searchable.

documents.name: Segments
documents.one_document: One segment in one project environment.
documents.title: The segment name, else its key.
documents.text: The name and description, `Project`, `Environment` and `Tags` lines, then the included and excluded users and contexts, then rule lines. A big segment's text says its membership is kept outside LaunchDarkly's API, and the members are not listed. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: The last change, else when the segment was created.

attributes.name: segment_key
attributes.text: The segment key. Searchable only when the segment has no name and the key is its title.

attributes.name: included, excluded, included_contexts, excluded_contexts
attributes.text: Users and contexts listed in the segment, so a query can find which segments include a user key. Big-segment membership is not listed.

attributes.name: Environment and segment references
attributes.text: Link the segment to its environment and to each segment its rules match. Not searchable as links.

attributes.name: created_at, last_modified_at
attributes.text: The last change, else creation, is the result date. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.launchdarkly_segment_key
attributes.text: The segment key. Picks out one segment. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The project key. Limits a query to one project. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The project name. Limits a query to one project by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
attributes.text: Always `project`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Project
attributes.text: The segment's project. Who can view the project decides who can read the segment. Not searchable.

documents.name: Environments
documents.title: The environment name, else its key.
documents.text: The name, `Project` and `Environment key` lines, `Marked critical`, `Requires confirmation for changes` and `Requires a comment on every change` when set, and a `Tags` line. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.launchdarkly_environment_key
attributes.text: The environment key. Picks out one environment. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The project key. Limits a query to one project. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The project name. Limits a query to one project by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
attributes.text: Always `project`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Project
attributes.text: The environment's project. Who can view the project decides who can read the environment. Not searchable.

documents.name: Members
documents.title: The first and last name, else the email, else `LaunchDarkly member`.
documents.text: The name, then `Email`, `Role`, `Custom roles` and `Teams` lines. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: email
attributes.text: The member's email, written as the `Email` line. Identifies the member as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: member_role, custom_roles
attributes.text: The base role and custom role keys, so a query can find who has which role.

attributes.name: teams
attributes.text: The member's team names, written as the `Teams` line. Links the member to each team's record.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.launchdarkly_member_id
attributes.text: The member id. Picks out one member. Not searchable.

documents.name: Teams
documents.title: The team name, else its key.
documents.text: The name, the description and a `Team key` line. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: team_key, description
attributes.text: The team key and its written purpose.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.launchdarkly_team_key
attributes.text: The team key. Picks out one team. Not searchable.

documents.name: Audit log entries
documents.title: The entry title as plain text, else its name, else `LaunchDarkly audit` with its id.
documents.text: The title, a `By` line with the member who made the change, the description, the short description when different, a `Comment` line, and one `Action` line per change with the action and the resource. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: member
attributes.text: The member who made the change, by name, else email, written as the `By` line. Links the entry to that member's record.

attributes.name: flags
attributes.text: The flags the entry touched, as `project/flag`, written in the `Action` lines. Links the entry to those flags. The entry is also linked to the environments, segments, members or teams it touched.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the change happened. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.launchdarkly_audit_id
attributes.text: The entry id. Picks out one entry. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Project
attributes.text: An entry about one project follows who can view that project. An entry about the account as a whole is not restricted. An entry about several projects carries a permission warning. Not searchable.

attributes.name: entry_kind, title_verb
attributes.text: LaunchDarkly's category for the entry and its verb phrase.

example_searches: Which flags does the beta-testers segment gate?
Who turned off the payments-v2 flag and what comment did they leave?
Which environments require a comment on every change?

connections: A flag to its maintainer member or maintainer team.
A flag to each environment it is configured in, and to each prerequisite flag.
A flag or segment to each segment its rules match.
A member to each of their teams.
An audit entry to the member who made it, and to the flags, environments, segments, members or teams it touched.
Links reach only items this connector has synced, that are not deleted, into the same database and collection.
No links to items in other tools.
people: A flag's maintainer and an audit entry's author are linked to member records, not attached to the item as people.
graph.from_text: Flag descriptions, audit comments and descriptions.

not_synced: Flags, segments and environments of projects you did not select.
Audit entries about a single project you did not select.
Per-user targeting values outside the flag configuration.
Custom flag properties, experiment definitions and goal ids.
Environment SDK keys and mobile keys, and members' MFA state and password status.
Metrics, experiments, releases and code references.
